supersededLiterals.rule: Every value this standard has ever RETIRED, as data. `npm run verify:spec-literals` fails the build when an agent-facing doc still asserts one of them, which is what stops the prose and the gate from disagreeing. When you change a value in this spec, add the old one here in the same commit — that is the whole maintenance cost, and it is what lets check A8 ("do not retype spec literals") be enforced by a machine instead of by a judge's prompt.
supersededLiterals.markerNote: A doc may still name a retired value ON PURPOSE — a "do not hardcode this" example, or a note recording the history. Put `superseded-ok` in a comment on that line to say so deliberately.

entries.why: MEASURED against the live host: the plugin iframe is 32px wider than the native settings column, so 16px padding lands content on the native edges. p-6 double-padded it and every row read visibly inset.
MEASURED: consecutive native settings sit ~24px apart. 32px read as too airy next to the host's own rhythm.
MEASURED: the host's own section labels are 14px / weight 700. 600 read visibly lighter beside them.
Same measurement as font-semibold, written as prose in the skill and the human doc. A weight is a number in prose and a utility in code; both spellings have to move together.

transparency.rule: A slide type is ALWAYS an iframe embedded in the presenter or audience app, so the HOST owns the background. Every surface this repo paints — html, body, #app, the view root, and any panel/card/row inside it — stays transparent. Never paint an opaque background at any level.
transparency.outlineLayerClass: pointer-events-none absolute inset-0 rounded-aha border border-current opacity-20
transparency.layerNote: Tailwind 3 does not generate opacity modifiers on currentColor (bg-current/10 emits nothing), so a deck-tracking tint or outline is a separate absolutely-positioned layer carrying bg-current/border-current plus an opacity-* utility. Its colour comes from the ink of the surface it sits in, so it follows the deck instead of painting a fixed grey.

autoHeight.canvasJustificationNote: A Canvas that opts INTO autoHeight states why in a comment on the line immediately above the call, starting with the marker "canvas autoHeight:". CHECK 7l reads that marker. Its first version instead scanned the 600 characters before the call for any `//` or `/*` — and because every file in this repo opens with a comment block, that window essentially always contained one, so the check could not fail. A machine-readable token is what makes an honest sentence close the finding deterministically; the same idea as slideAttributes.justificationMarker.
autoHeight.note: Settings and Audience are content-height iframes: the host shrink-wraps them from the height the plugin reports, so both ALWAYS pass { autoHeight: true } explicitly — relying on the default silently loses it the moment someone passes an options object without the field. The Canvas normally lives inside the host's fixed 16:9 stage and must NOT report a content height; turn it on only when the slide type's purpose genuinely calls for a content-driven canvas, and say why at the call site.

settings.labelClass: mb-1 flex items-center gap-1 text-sm font-bold text-aha-panel-ink
settings.inkNote: The settings panel is embedded in the host EDITOR panel, which is fixed app chrome rather than a deck-themed surface — so its ink stays a fixed brand token (the aha-settings-label / text-aha-indigo family). Ink still tracks whatever the background tracks; here that background is the host's own panel, not the deck.
settings.labelTooltipRule: Every label may carry a trailing info icon whose tooltip states the constraint or caveat — that is the host pattern: on a native slide EVERY settings label ("Câu hỏi của bạn", "Đáp án", "Điểm", "Giới hạn thời gian", "Bảng xếp hạng") has one. Use it wherever a rule is worth stating; keep the copy inside tooltipMaxWidthPx.
settings.hostPanelAlignment: MEASURED on the live staging presenter (1600px viewport): the native settings column runs x=1127..1478 (351px) and its section labels sit flush at x=1127, because the host panel supplies the outer padding. The plugin iframe is 383px wide — 32px wider than that column — so a 16px horizontal padding (p-4) lands the plugin content on exactly the native edges. p-6 (the pre-v6 value) double-padded it: content came out 335px wide and visibly inset from every native row.
settings.hostLabelReference: MEASURED: section label = 14px / weight 700 / rgb(75,75,75); a single-row setting label with a leading icon = 14px / weight 400, inset 22px. The pre-v6 standard said 600 / #3E3E5A, which read wrong next to the host's own labels.
settings.fieldGapReference: MEASURED: two consecutive single-row settings ("Giới hạn thời gian" -> "Bảng xếp hạng") have label tops 63px apart with ~40px rows, i.e. ~24px between blocks. mb-8 (32px) read as too airy against the host.
settings.legacyLabelClassNote: `.aha-settings-label` in main.css (text-sm font-semibold text-aha-indigo) is the PRE-v6 class and is left untouched on purpose: it is shared by every existing panel, and rewriting it would restyle slide types this standard has not audited. New and rebuilt panels use labelClass above.

colour.rule: On Canvas and Audience, EVERY colour — text, any surface treatment, any mark — comes from the deck theme the host passes down. A slide type does not invent colour. Only the three exceptions below may sit outside the theme, and a user prompt that explicitly asks for a specific colour is the only way to add a fourth.

themeXprops.slide.textColour: The ink the deck author chose. All text and icon colour on Canvas and Audience tracks this.
themeXprops.slide.baseColour: The deck background colour. Read it to REASON about the backdrop (contrast decisions); never to repaint it — nothing in a slide type paints a background. Presenter surface only.
themeXprops.presentationColorPalette: The deck accent palette (auto-padded to 30 entries). Marks — bar fills, chart segments, chips, team colours — index into this.
themeXprops.presentationLighterColorPalette: Lighter variants of the same palette, for a second tier of marks.
themeXprops.presentation.fontFamily: The deck font. Safe to inherit everywhere: it changes shape, not contrast.

allowedExceptions: A FALLBACK for when the host sends nothing: `slideProps.textColour ?? ahaBrand.space`. The theme value always wins when present.

A SEMANTIC signal — correct/incorrect, success/error/warning/info — from src/iframe/brandTokens.ts. Success must read as success in every deck, which a deck accent cannot promise. Pair it with a non-colour cue.
An explicit instruction in the user prompt naming a specific colour or treatment. Note it in a comment at the call site so the next reader knows it was asked for, not invented.
forbiddenOnCanvasAndAudience: raw hex / rgb() / hsl() / named CSS colours
aha-* Tailwind colour utilities (text-aha-*, bg-aha-*, border-aha-*, ring-aha-*) — those are bundled brand colours, not the deck theme
a self-computed "adapt to the theme" guess (luminance flips, derived tints) instead of reading the theme
colour.workbenchLimit: The playground broker seeds presentationColorPalette*, fontFamily and language but NOT slide.textColour / slide.baseColour, so locally the fallback renders. Verify theme behaviour in the product apps.

canvas.framedRootClass: flex h-full w-full flex-col bg-transparent p-6
canvas.markColourRule: A mark carries deck colour: index presentationColorPalette by item position (palette[i % palette.length]) so each option keeps a stable, deck-derived colour, and the room sees ITS OWN palette rather than one accent for everything. presentationLighterColorPalette is the second tier. A SEMANTIC marker (leader, correct) stays a bundled token.

audience.tapRowClass: relative flex w-full items-center gap-3 rounded-aha px-4 py-3 text-left
audience.submittedCardClass: relative flex flex-col items-center gap-2 rounded-aha p-6 text-center
audience.markColourRule: The selected / submitted state of a tappable takes its accent from presentationColorPalette by the option position, matching what the canvas paints for that option.

slideAttributes.rule: A slide attribute is schema you own forever — migrated, persisted and reasoned about on every read. Before adding a field, check whether the HOST already provides it behind an `enable*` flag, then whether an existing field already carries the information. A new field is the last resort and needs a stated reason.
decisionOrder: 1. HOST SETTING — is it already provided behind an `enable*` flag? Turn the flag on in OVERRIDES (scripts/generate-slide-types-api.mjs) and read the value off slideProps. Add no field and no control. Inventory: the reuse-host-capabilities skill.
2. EXISTING FIELD — does a field on this config already carry it? Derive from that instead of storing a second copy that can disagree.
3. NEW FIELD — only now, and say in a comment why neither of the above fit.

hostSettingByNeed.title / question: enableQuestionTitle → read slideProps.title (+ `titleField` in metadata.ts names the config field the host writes into)
hostSettingByNeed.subtitle / description: enableQuestionDescription → the host renders the description field under the title
hostSettingByNeed.question image: enableQuestionImage → the host renders its own image picker for the question
hostSettingByNeed.countdown / duration: enableTimeLimit → read slideProps.timeToAnswer; do not run your own timer authority
hostSettingByNeed.close / lock submissions: enableStopSubmitssionSetting (doubled s — see spellingTrap) → read slideProps.stopSubmission
hostSettingByNeed.vote / response count: DEPRECATED (enableVoteCount / setSubmissionCount) — the host reads audiences_response_count, set automatically from the backend; report nothing
hostSettingByNeed.\"Other settings\" section heading: enableLabelOtherSetting → the host draws the heading + divider the other Other-settings controls sit under. NOT an "Other" answer choice. Turn it on whenever you enable any control in that group, or your checkbox floats heading-less (AHA-323)
hostSettingByNeed.profanity filter on responses: enableFilteringProfanitySetting → the host renders the filter toggle; also see filterProfaneWords() on xprops
hostSettingByNeed.audience attaches an image to their answ: enableImageSubmissionSetting → the host renders the image-submission toggle + upload path
hostSettingByNeed.show live results on the audience device: enableShowVotingResultsOnAudienceVisible → the host renders the toggle; do not build your own "show results" switch
hostSettingByNeed.cap votes per participant: enableVotesPerParticipantSetting → the host renders the max-votes input
hostSettingByNeed.extra fields on the submission form: enableAdditionalFieldsSetting → the host renders the additional-fields editor
hostSettingByNeed.participant identity (name / emoji / tea: enableAudienceJoinPresentation → the host runs the QR/join flow and hands you audienceName / audienceEmoji / team. Never prompt for identity yourself
hostSettingByNeed.lobby + Start before a scored round: enableGameLobby → the host runs the lobby; gate your round on slideProps.quizStatus, never on presentation.presenting
hostSettingByNeed.moderate submissions before they appear: enableModerateQuestion → the host runs its native approval queue. Replaces any per-slide requireApproval toggle
hostSettingByNeed.full-canvas / edge-to-edge layout: enableFullScreen → the host hides its title bar and gives the iframe the whole viewport. Must agree with metadata `fullscreenCanvas` and the canvas root

slideAttributes.enableOnlyWhatYouUse: Turning a flag on "just in case" puts a control in the host editor that does nothing. Enable what the slide type actually consumes.
slideAttributes.exception: A field is justified when no host setting expresses the concept (how this slide lays out or reveals its own results, its own option list, its mechanic knobs) — or when the user prompt explicitly asks for a separate field. State which, at the field.
slideAttributes.justificationNote: When a field genuinely cannot reuse a host setting, write the reason in a comment on (or directly above) the field, starting with the marker "no host setting:". The audit reads it and stops asking — so the rule costs one honest sentence rather than a suppression list, and the reason stays next to the field for the next reader.
slideAttributes.emissionNote: defaultSettings() in scripts/generate-slide-types-api.mjs declares the keys in defaultSettingKeys as false and then spreads the OVERRIDES entry over them. So a key from optInOnlyKeys still reaches the manifest when you set it — it is simply absent (rather than false) on slides that do not. Setting any flag from either list works the same way.
slideAttributes.spellingTrap: The close-submissions flag exists in TWO spellings and the manifest emits both: defaultSettings() declares enableStopSubmissionSetting (single s) as false, while every working slide sets enableStopSubmitssionSetting (doubled s) in OVERRIDES — that doubled-s form is the production spelling the host actually reads. Setting the single-s key to true does nothing. Copy the doubled-s form verbatim.
slideAttributes.iframePreloadNote: Iframe preload is host-side. reuse-host-capabilities lists enableIframePreload, while sample-slide/types.ts records "no direct enable* key" for it — the two disagree, so verify against the host before relying on the flag.

settingsLibrary.rule: Composed, reusable settings controls live in src/iframe/settings and are imported from '@/iframe/settings'. They are COMPOSITIONS over the themed Ant primitives (and a couple of shapes Ant has no built-in for), not replacements: a plain <Input>/<Switch>/<Select> already carries the storybook look, so use those directly. Reach for a library component when you need the composed LAYOUT, a specific repeatable pattern, or a shape Ant lacks. All are pure Vue + Ant (no cross-slide-type imports), so they stay production-portable like the rest of @/iframe/*.
settingsLibrary.governance: A component earns a place here only if it composes primitives or enforces a guardrail. Plain pass-throughs stay documented conventions, not wrappers.

components.SectionHeader: Bold (700, host-measured) header of a group or a master-toggle row; optional (?) tooltip + right-aligned action slot.
components.SettingRow: One standalone control with a 400-weight label (single controls are never bold); inline (label left / control right) or stack (control full-width below); optional (?) tooltip and help line.
components.SubSettingGroup: Indent-only (mt-4 pl-4, no left rail) wrapper for settings that apply only when their parent toggle is on. Parent must be a SectionHeader.
components.ModeField: A labelled field whose input changes with an inline mode switch: label + a small exclusive control (outline RadioButton group — purple border/text when selected, NEVER a solid fill — or Ant Segmented) share the top row; the body renders the slot matching the selected mode and swaps in place. The 'Front label: [Text|Image]' pattern. Enforces that ONLY the active mode's body is rendered, so a hidden mode holds no live control. Slot names must match the option values.
components.ImageDropzone: Standalone full-width image field styled to match the storybook LocalFileUploader (2px dashed grey card on a faint grey fill, lavender hover border + focus ring, a 16px PictureOutlined image icon (the OptionRow/ImageActionButton glyph) in secondary ink #4B4B4B) with empty/loading/filled states; the large-format sibling of ImageActionButton. Filled = the image in a fixed grey display box, fitted (portrait/landscape/smaller all handled via fit=contain by default, never stretched or cropped; fit=cover crops to fill), with a Change / Edit / Delete overlay on hover. Emits intents (select/change/edit/remove, and drop(File)); the slide type runs the HOST modals (openUploadImageModal / openEditImageModal / uploadImage), never a self-built uploader. NOT Ant's a-upload-dragger (which performs the upload). SETTINGS ONLY (the card paints a faint surface).
components.OptionRow: Repeatable option/answer row ported from the Ranking slide: drag handle, optional correct-answer toggle, borderless textarea with hover char-counter, optional image control, floating delete. Image parts toggle via showImage/allowCorrect.
components.ImageActionButton: Per-option image control with every state: empty (add) / loading (spinner while the host modal opens) / thumbnail with hover overlay + Change/Edit/Delete menu. Emits intents; the slide type runs the host modals.
components.CountedInput: Single-line text field with a FOCUS-ONLY character counter, done the safe way: the counter is always in the DOM as a sibling, hidden at rest and revealed via the container's :focus-within, so the AntD Input's DOM never rebuilds on focus and the caret is never dropped. Use this (or OptionRow for lists) for any capped rename/label field — NEVER reactively toggle AntD :show-count on @focus (it remounts the input and breaks click/focus; AHAM-463). Composes inside a SettingRow, which supplies the label; forwards data-testid/aria-* to the native input.
components.CardSelect: Single-select as an icon+label card grid — the one selection shape Ant has no built-in for. Ported from budget-allocation-v2's chart picker.
components.NumberWithUnit: Number (native digit input with a hover-revealed ▲/▼ stepper that steps by `step` and clamps to min/max; hard-capped at `maxDigits` digits — default 4, a 5th keystroke/paste is ignored) + unit-written-in-full + optional `errorMessage` reason line below the field + optional quick-preset select, at an 8px corner. For durations/numbers-with-a-unit, not a Segmented. Reuse the host countdown (enableTimeLimit) when the concept is a standard time limit.
components.HelpTooltip: The trailing (?) info affordance on a label: Ant Tooltip + question-mark icon, copy capped to ~2 lines.
components.DropdownMenu: Themed action menu (<a-dropdown> + <a-menu>) with neutral-grey item hover; used for the image Change/Edit/Delete menu and any Improve-style action menu.
components.InfoBox: Callout/notice box (information/success/warning/error), optionally closable with localStorage-persisted dismissal. Replicates the storybook InfoBox (bespoke, not Ant Alert). SETTINGS ONLY — it paints a tinted background, which is fine in the host editor chrome but not on Canvas/Audience.
components.QuestionList: Editable list of collapsible questions (Ant Collapse), each with a prompt field (SectionHeader + Input) and answer choices rendered as OptionRow (correct toggle, optional image). Per-question delete is a tertiary icon button with a capped, iframe-safe tooltip. v-model the questions array; single/multiple/none correct modes; image picking emitted as an intent.
components.NumberedItem: A repeatable, numbered SECTION wrapper for a settings list whose items are COMPOSITES - each holds a body of fields and/or a nested option list plus its own delete, not a single value. Owns only the muted grey number chip (sequence identity), the '<Label> N' header, a TERTIARY (type=text, borderless, non-danger) delete shown on hover of the whole item (drop it entirely with deletable=false), and the secondary-fill grey container that wraps the WHOLE item - chip, label, delete and body together (variant 'contained' default; 'plain' = no fill, for single-field items). The body is a DEFAULT SLOT - compose OptionRow/ModeField/any Ant control inside; it never rebuilds them. USE when the creator builds a countable set of composite items whose ordinal they refer to (Question, Blank, Card, Hotspot, Round). DON'T use for a flat list of single values (that is OptionRow directly, numbered ONLY per SETTINGS-39), for a one-off object (just its fields), or for a collapsible numbered question+choices accordion (that is QuestionList, which composes this).

conventions.note: These stay plain Ant, documented here rather than wrapped.
conventions.segmented: Not part of the rulebook — raw <a-segmented> (unstyled Ant) if a slide ever needs it; no guidance, no wrapper.
conventions.radioGroup: 2–4 exclusive modes as buttons: <RadioGroup button-style="outline"> + <RadioButton> (purple border + text on the selected button, NO solid fill). Outline is the Ant default; the solid fill is retired.
conventions.radioDot: A choose-1 list where each option needs describing: dot <a-radio>. Themed to the native aha-radio look (grey ring #B4BCCF, purple-40 dot #A96FF0, 3px halo) via storybook-overrides.css GAP 7 — no wrapper component.

settingsRulebook.rule: Canonical patterns for the recurring settings across all slide types, from a source survey (not memory). The repo-specific source of truth the settings build guidance, the aha-design-settings-judge Part A, and the audit lints all read. Cross-product UX laws (help-text discipline, noun-phrase names, group size, dangerous actions) are NOT duplicated here — they live in the aha-design-settings plugin skill; this section owns only the repo-specific choices.
settingsRulebook.compose: Every field composes a library component (SectionHeader / SettingRow / OptionRow / QuestionList / NumberWithUnit / InfoBox / DropdownMenu) — never hand-rolled markup.

labelAnatomy.leadingIconNote: Setting labels carry NO decorative leading icon (star/trophy/clock/etc.) — a label is text + optional (?) tooltip + control. Enforced by construction (SectionHeader/SettingRow expose no icon slot) and by the decorative-icon audit lint.
labelAnatomy.help: Default a label's explanation to the (?) tooltip. An inline help line appears ONLY when the slide creator explicitly asks for one.

controls.radioGroup: 2–4 exclusive modes → <RadioGroup button-style="outline"> + <RadioButton>. Outline (purple border+text, no solid fill) is the default; solid is retired.
controls.segmented: Not in the rulebook — raw <a-segmented> if ever needed; no guidance.
controls.number: A bare number → <InputNumber>. A number WITH a unit (duration, points) → <NumberWithUnit>; the unit is set by the plugin (default 'seconds' for time, 'points' for scoring) and only changes when the creator explicitly asks.
controls.optionList: A repeatable option/answer list → <OptionRow> (flat) or <QuestionList> (question groups) — never a hand-rolled row. min 2, drag-reorder on, correct-answer toggle on for scored slides.

recurringSettings.note: For each recurring setting: host-native (reuse the enable* flag, never rebuild) vs plugin field, and the canonical control.
recurringSettings.timeLimit: Whole-slide countdown → host-native (enableTimeLimit, read slideProps.timeToAnswer). A per-round / per-question / game timer the host flag cannot express → plugin field via <NumberWithUnit> (unit flexible). Label 'Time limit' + (?) tooltip.
recurringSettings.scoring: Group Points + Faster-answers + Leaderboard under one 'Scoring' SectionHeader. Points → <NumberWithUnit> unit 'points'; the field schema follows the slide's own rule (do NOT force a rigid min/max), but consolidate field names when the same concept is spelled differently and it does not affect the user. Faster-answers (speedBonus) → SettingRow + Switch. Leaderboard → a plugin toggle shown in the Scoring section when the slide has scoring.
recurringSettings.numberedItems: A countable set of COMPOSITE items the creator refers to by ordinal (Blank 1, Card 2, Round 3) — each item a body of fields and/or its own option list — wraps each item in <NumberedItem> (muted grey chip + '<Label> N' header + tertiary type=text delete + secondary-fill grey container). Per SETTINGS-39: a GROUP of composite items gets numbered this way; a plain unordered list of single values does NOT get numbers — that is <OptionRow> directly. Compose the item body into NumberedItem's default slot; never rebuild the chip/header/delete per slide type.
recurringSettings.sound: Audio tied to the question is host-owned; a standalone per-slide sound toggle → plugin (SettingRow + Switch).

settingsRulebook.decorativeIconNote: The audit warns when a Settings.vue imports one of these as a leading label icon. Functional icons that live INSIDE the library components (Plus/Delete/Info/Question/Picture/Holder) are fine and not listed.
settingsRulebook.grandfather: These rules apply to NEW / rebuilt slide types. The existing slide types predate the rulebook (e.g. all use button-style="solid"); they are grandfathered and migrate opportunistically — the lints WARN, they do not fail the build.
settingsRulebook.crossProductUX: For noun-phrase naming, help-text discipline, tooltip constraints, group size/header, no-mixed-toggle, dependent sub-settings, plan-gating and dangerous-action patterns, see the aha-design-settings plugin skill (and aha-design-settings-judge Part B) — this repo does not restate them.
